---
title: "Store Sales: Statistical Time-Series Analysis and Forecasting"
author: "AMS 586"
output:
  pdf_document:
    latex_engine: xelatex
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 1
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 1
abstract: |
  This report studies grocery sales at aggregate and store-family levels,
  then develops interpretable 16-day forecasts using regression with SARIMA
  errors. It distinguishes missing calendar dates from genuine zero sales,
  evaluates trend and seasonality with STL, ACF/PACF and stationarity tests,
  and checks one-step innovations and model stability. Final estimation uses
  all observed training history; a bounded likelihood-based search and explicit
  fallbacks cover every test series. Remaining dependence and the absence of
  observed test targets limit claims about model adequacy and Kaggle accuracy.
fontsize: 12pt
geometry: margin=1in
header-includes:
  - \usepackage{booktabs}
  - \newsavebox{\reporttablebox}
  - \raggedbottom
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, dev.args = list(pointsize = 11), out.width = "100%", fig.align = "center", comment = NA,
                      warning = TRUE, message = FALSE)
if (!requireNamespace("urca", quietly = TRUE))
  stop("Install the required package with install.packages('urca').")
options(width = 110)
report_series_label <- function(x) {
  old <- c("Seasonally adjusted log total", "Differenced adjusted log total", "Example training log sales", "Example first difference", "Example weekly difference")
  new <- c("Adjusted log", "Diff. adjusted log", "Example log", "Example first diff.", "Example weekly diff.")
  for (i in seq_along(old)) x <- gsub(old[i], new[i], x, fixed = TRUE)
  x
}
# Presentation helpers only: never used by model fitting or forecasting.
report_table <- function(x, title = NULL, digits = 3, col.names = names(x), alignment = NULL) {
  old_na <- getOption("knitr.kable.NA"); options(knitr.kable.NA = "--")
  on.exit(options(knitr.kable.NA = old_na), add = TRUE)
  if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
    cat("\n\n\\par\\noindent\\begin{minipage}{\\linewidth}\n")
    if (!is.null(title)) cat("\\textbf{", knitr:::escape_latex(title), "}\\par\\smallskip\n", sep = "")
    tab <- as.character(knitr::kable(x, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE,
      digits = digits, col.names = col.names, row.names = FALSE, linesep = "", escape = TRUE))
    if (!is.null(alignment)) {
      lines <- strsplit(tab, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
      j <- grep("\\begin{tabular}", lines, fixed = TRUE)
      lines[j] <- paste0("\\begin{tabular}{", alignment, "}")
      tab <- paste(lines, collapse = "\n")
    }
    cat("\\begin{center}\n\\begingroup\\small\n\\sbox{\\reporttablebox}{%\n", tab,
        "}\n\\ifdim\\wd\\reporttablebox>\\linewidth\n",
        "\\resizebox{\\linewidth}{!}{\\usebox{\\reporttablebox}}\n",
        "\\else\\usebox{\\reporttablebox}\\fi\n\\endgroup\n\\end{center}\n",
        "\\end{minipage}\\par\\medskip\n\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    if (!is.null(title)) cat("\n\n**", title, "**\n\n", sep = "")
    cat(as.character(knitr::kable(x, format = "pipe", digits = digits,
      col.names = col.names, row.names = FALSE)), "\n\n")
  }
  invisible(x)
}
report_p <- function(p) format.pval(p, digits = 3, eps = .001)
report_decision <- function(x) ifelse(x, "R", "NR")
report_stationarity <- function(tab, title = "Stationarity tests at 5%") {
  groups <- split(seq_len(nrow(tab)), factor(tab$series, levels = unique(tab$series)))
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(groups, function(i) {
    z <- tab[i, ]; a <- z[1, ]; short <- z[z$KPSS_bandwidth == "short", ][1, ]
    long <- z[z$KPSS_bandwidth == "long", ][1, ]
    data.frame(Series = report_series_label(a$series),
      Terms = if (a$deterministic == "intercept + trend") "Trend" else "Constant",
      ADF = sprintf("%.3f (%d)", a$ADF_stat, a$ADF_lag),
      `ADF 5%` = report_decision(a$ADF_reject),
      `KPSS short` = sprintf("%.3f (%d)", short$KPSS_stat, short$KPSS_lag),
      `KPSS long` = sprintf("%.3f (%d)", long$KPSS_stat, long$KPSS_lag),
      `KPSS S/L` = paste(report_decision(short$KPSS_reject), report_decision(long$KPSS_reject), sep = "/"),
      check.names = FALSE)
  }))
  report_table(out, title, digits = 3)
  critical <- unique(tab[c("deterministic", "ADF_critical_5pct", "KPSS_critical_5pct")])
  cat("R = reject; NR = do not reject. Parentheses give the selected ADF lag or KPSS bandwidth. ")
  cat("Trend includes an intercept. Critical values (ADF / KPSS): ",
    paste(sprintf("%s: %.3f / %.3f", critical$deterministic,
      critical$ADF_critical_5pct, critical$KPSS_critical_5pct), collapse = "; "), ".\n\n", sep = "")
  invisible(out)
}
report_orders <- function(f) {
  if (inherits(f, "lm")) return("iid")
  a <- f$arma
  sprintf("(%d,%d,%d)(%d,%d,%d)", a[1], a[6], a[2], a[3], a[7], a[4])
}
report_model_comparison <- function(detail) {
  models <- unique(c("M1", "M1_raw", "M2", "M3_base", detail$selected))
  tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(models, function(m) {
    f <- detail$result$fits[[m]]
    if (is.null(f)) return(NULL)
    raw <- identical(m, "M1_raw")
    if (inherits(f, "lm")) {
      k <- attr(logLik(f), "df"); n <- nobs(f)
      aicc <- if (raw) NA_real_ else AIC(f) + 2 * k * (k + 1) / (n - k - 1)
      bic <- if (raw) NA_real_ else BIC(f)
      conv <- "OLS"
    } else { aicc <- f$aicc; bic <- f$bic; conv <- as.character(f$code) }
    cn <- names(coef(f))
    K <- if (any(grepl("annual_sin3", cn, fixed = TRUE))) 3L else
      if (any(grepl("annual_sin2", cn, fixed = TRUE))) 2L else
      if (any(grepl("annual_sin", cn, fixed = TRUE))) 1L else NA_integer_
    d <- detail$result$diagnostics[[m]]
    pv <- function(h) if (!is.null(d) && nrow(d)) d$p_value[match(h, d$lag)] else NA_real_
    data.frame(Model = m, Errors = report_orders(f), K = K,
      AICc = round(aicc, 2), BIC = round(bic, 2), Conv. = conv,
      `LB 14` = report_p(pv(14)), `LB 28` = report_p(pv(28)), check.names = FALSE)
  }))
  report_table(tab, "Representative fitted-model comparison (seasonal period 7)", digits = 2)
  cat("Convergence code 0 denotes successful numerical optimization. Raw-scale OLS information criteria are omitted because its response scale differs. ")
  cat("Compare criteria only for the same response data and differencing/likelihood convention.\n\n")
  eligible <- !tab$Model %in% c("M1", "M1_raw")
  if (any(eligible)) cat("Among these SARIMA specifications, AICc favors **",
    tab$Model[which(eligible)[which.min(tab$AICc[eligible])]], "**; BIC favors **",
    tab$Model[which(eligible)[which.min(tab$BIC[eligible])]],
    "**. This expresses an in-sample fit/complexity tradeoff, not an accuracy comparison.\n\n", sep = "")
  invisible(tab)
}
```

\clearpage

# 1. Data and quality checks

Daily sales are forecast for individual store-product-family combinations over
August 16-31, 2017. All available training observations through August 15 are
used for final fitting. Test data supply only identifiers, dates and known
promotion counts; hidden test sales and unavailable future transactions/oil
prices are not used. No validation split is introduced.

```{r read-data, include=FALSE}
data_dir <- Sys.getenv("STORE_SALES_DATA", "store-sales-time-series-forecasting")
if (!dir.exists(data_dir)) stop("Knit from the Kaggle folder containing the data directory.")
csv_files <- sort(list.files(data_dir, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE))
datasets <- setNames(lapply(csv_files, function(path) {
  x <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if ("date" %in% names(x)) x$date <- as.Date(x$date)
  x
}), tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(csv_files)))
required <- c("train", "test", "stores", "oil", "holidays_events",
              "transactions", "sample_submission")
stopifnot(all(required %in% names(datasets)))
train <- datasets$train; test <- datasets$test; stores <- datasets$stores
oil <- datasets$oil; holidays_events <- datasets$holidays_events
transactions <- datasets$transactions; sample_submission <- datasets$sample_submission
inventory <- data.frame(dataset = names(datasets),
  rows = vapply(datasets, nrow, integer(1)),
  columns = vapply(datasets, ncol, integer(1)),
  column_names = vapply(datasets, function(x) paste(names(x), collapse = ", "), ""))
knitr::kable(inventory, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r report-inventory, results='asis'}
report_inventory <- inventory
report_inventory$dataset <- gsub("_", " ", report_inventory$dataset)
report_table(report_inventory, "Input datasets", col.names = c("Dataset", "Rows", "Columns", "Column names"),
  alignment = "p{2.7cm}rrp{8.1cm}")
```

```{r missing-values-and-duplicates, include=FALSE}
missingness <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(datasets), function(nm) {
  x <- datasets[[nm]]
  data.frame(dataset = nm, column = names(x), missing = colSums(is.na(x)),
             percent = 100 * colSums(is.na(x)) / nrow(x), row.names = NULL)
}))
knitr::kable(missingness, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
keys <- list(train = c("date", "store_nbr", "family"),
  test = c("date", "store_nbr", "family"), stores = "store_nbr", oil = "date",
  holidays_events = c("date", "type", "locale", "locale_name", "description", "transferred"),
  transactions = c("date", "store_nbr"), sample_submission = "id")
duplicate_report <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(keys), function(nm) {
  x <- datasets[[nm]]
  data.frame(dataset = nm, key = paste(keys[[nm]], collapse = ", "),
    duplicate_key_rows = sum(duplicated(x[keys[[nm]]])),
    exact_duplicate_rows = sum(duplicated(x)))
}))
knitr::kable(duplicate_report, row.names = FALSE)
id_duplicates <- data.frame(dataset = c("train", "test", "sample_submission"),
  duplicated_id = sapply(datasets[c("train", "test", "sample_submission")],
                         function(x) sum(duplicated(x$id))))
knitr::kable(id_duplicates, row.names = FALSE)
# Duplicated training keys would make aggregate totals ambiguous.
if (duplicate_report$duplicate_key_rows[duplicate_report$dataset == "train"] > 0L)
  stop("Resolve duplicate training keys before continuing.")
```
```{r date-continuity, include=FALSE}
dated_names <- names(datasets)[vapply(datasets, function(x) "date" %in% names(x), TRUE)]
missing_dates <- setNames(lapply(dated_names, function(nm) {
  d <- sort(unique(na.omit(datasets[[nm]]$date)))
  seq(min(d), max(d), by = "day")[!seq(min(d), max(d), by = "day") %in% d]
}), dated_names)
coverage <- do.call(rbind, lapply(dated_names, function(nm) {
  d <- datasets[[nm]]$date
  data.frame(dataset = nm, start = min(d, na.rm = TRUE), end = max(d, na.rm = TRUE),
    observed_dates = length(unique(na.omit(d))), missing_calendar_dates = length(missing_dates[[nm]]),
    missing_date_values = sum(is.na(d)))
}))
knitr::kable(coverage, row.names = FALSE)
# Lists the actual missing dates, not only their counts.
lapply(missing_dates, as.character)
```

```{r report-data-quality, results='asis'}
report_table(missingness[missingness$missing > 0, ], "Columns with missing values", digits = 2,
  col.names = c("Dataset", "Column", "Missing", "Percent"))
cat(sprintf("All other %d columns have zero missing values. Missing sales are never filled with zero; genuine zero sales remain observations.\n\n",
  sum(missingness$missing == 0)))
report_duplicates <- duplicate_report
report_duplicates$dataset <- gsub("_", " ", report_duplicates$dataset)
report_duplicates$key <- c("Event descriptors", "Date", "ID", "Store", "Date/store/family", "Date/store/family", "Date/store")[match(report_duplicates$dataset,
  c("holidays events", "oil", "sample submission", "stores", "test", "train", "transactions"))]
report_table(report_duplicates, "Duplicate-record checks", col.names = c("Dataset", "Key", "Extra key rows", "Exact duplicates"))
cat("Holiday keys use date, type, locale, locale name, description and transfer status; multiple events on one date need not be duplicates. ")
cat(paste(sprintf("%s ID duplicates: %d", id_duplicates$dataset, id_duplicates$duplicated_id), collapse = "; "), ".\n\n", sep = "")
report_coverage <- coverage
report_coverage$dataset <- gsub("_", " ", report_coverage$dataset)
report_table(report_coverage, "Date coverage and absent calendar dates", col.names = c("Dataset", "First date", "Last date", "Dates", "Absent dates", "Missing date values"))
cat("**Absent training dates:** ", paste(as.character(missing_dates$train), collapse = ", "), ".\n\n", sep = "")
```

The holiday table records events rather than a daily measurement process, and
oil observations are not expected on every calendar date. Their absent-date
counts are retained above, but exhaustive date lists do not identify additional
data errors. Missing dates, missing recorded values and observed zeros are
separate concepts throughout the analysis.

```{r aggregate-sales-and-completeness, include=FALSE}
valid_identity <- complete.cases(train[c("date", "store_nbr", "family")])
cat("Training rows omitted for missing date/store/family:", sum(!valid_identity), "\n")
t <- train[valid_identity, ]
cat("Rows with missing sales:", sum(is.na(t$sales)),
    "; actual zero-sales rows preserved:", sum(t$sales == 0, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
pairs <- unique(t[c("store_nbr", "family")])
expected_pairs <- nrow(pairs)
# A daily total is retained only when all expected series have observed sales.
# An incomplete day's partial sum is not an estimate of its total.
by_date <- split(seq_len(nrow(t)), t$date)
daily <- do.call(rbind, lapply(by_date, function(i) {
  x <- t[i, ]
  data.frame(date = x$date[1], rows = nrow(x), missing_sales = sum(is.na(x$sales)),
    sales = if (nrow(x) == expected_pairs && !anyNA(x$sales)) sum(x$sales) else NA_real_,
    promotion = if (nrow(x) == expected_pairs && !anyNA(x$onpromotion)) sum(x$onpromotion) else NA_real_)
}))
calendar <- data.frame(date = seq(min(daily$date), max(daily$date), by = "day"))
daily_sales <- merge(calendar, daily, by = "date", all.x = TRUE, sort = TRUE)
cat("Missing calendar dates:", sum(is.na(daily_sales$rows)),
    "; observed but incomplete sales days:", sum(!is.na(daily_sales$rows) & is.na(daily_sales$sales)),
    "; days omitted from complete-day summaries:", sum(is.na(daily_sales$sales)), "\n")
longest_segment <- function(date, value) {
  stopifnot(!is.unsorted(date), !anyDuplicated(date))
  good <- !is.na(value)
  runs <- rle(good)
  ends <- cumsum(runs$lengths)
  candidates <- which(runs$values)
  if (!length(candidates)) stop("No complete observations.")
  k <- candidates[which.max(runs$lengths[candidates])]
  i <- seq.int(ends[k] - runs$lengths[k] + 1L, ends[k])
  stopifnot(all(diff(as.numeric(date[i])) == 1))
  list(index = i, date = date[i], value = value[i], omitted = length(value) - length(i))
}
segment <- longest_segment(daily_sales$date, daily_sales$sales)
cat("Regular analysis segment:", as.character(min(segment$date)), "through",
    as.character(max(segment$date)), "; n =", length(segment$value),
    "; dates outside segment =", segment$omitted, "\n")
stopifnot(length(segment$value) >= 60)
```
```{r descriptive-statistics, include=FALSE}
describe <- function(x) {
  omitted <- sum(is.na(x)); x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  c(n = length(x), omitted = omitted, mean = mean(x), median = median(x),
    variance = var(x), sd = sd(x), minimum = min(x),
    Q1 = unname(quantile(x, .25)), Q3 = unname(quantile(x, .75)), maximum = max(x))
}
knitr::kable(rbind(training_record_sales = describe(train$sales),
                   daily_total_sales = describe(daily_sales$sales)), digits = 3)
zero_days <- daily_sales[!is.na(daily_sales$sales) & daily_sales$sales == 0, c("date", "sales")]
cat("Days with observed zero total sales:", nrow(zero_days), "\n")
knitr::kable(zero_days, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r report-sales-summary, results='asis'}
report_desc <- rbind(training_record_sales = describe(train$sales), daily_total_sales = describe(daily_sales$sales))
report_desc_display <- data.frame(Statistic = colnames(report_desc), check.names = FALSE)
for (j in seq_len(nrow(report_desc))) report_desc_display[[c("Record sales", "Daily total")[j]]] <-
  ifelse(colnames(report_desc) %in% c("n", "omitted"), format(round(report_desc[j, ]), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE),
         formatC(report_desc[j, ], format = "g", digits = 5))
report_table(report_desc_display, "Record-level and aggregate daily sales summaries")
cat(sprintf("Training rows omitted for missing date/store/family: %d; rows with missing sales: %d; genuine zero-sales records retained: %s. ",
  sum(!valid_identity), sum(is.na(t$sales)), format(sum(t$sales == 0, na.rm = TRUE), big.mark = ",")))
cat(sprintf("Observed days with zero aggregate sales: %d. Incomplete/absent daily totals: %d.\n\n", nrow(zero_days), sum(is.na(daily_sales$sales))))
cat(sprintf("**Regular EDA segment:** %s to %s (%d consecutive daily observations). It excludes %d observed daily totals outside that segment. ",
  min(segment$date), max(segment$date), length(segment$value), sum(!is.na(daily_sales$sales) & !daily_sales$date %in% segment$date)))
cat("The one-year EDA segment is not assumed representative of the whole history. **Final forecasting retains the complete training calendar**, treating absent targets as NA in the state-space likelihood, not as zero.\n\n")
```

# 2. Aggregate exploratory analysis

```{r plot-sales, echo=FALSE, fig.height=4}
plot(daily_sales$date, daily_sales$sales, type = "l", col = "steelblue",
     main = "Daily Total Sales: All Stores and Families", xlab = "Date", ylab = "Sales (units)")
```

The aggregate trajectory shows changing sales levels and pronounced calendar
variation. Distributional and mean-variance comparisons motivate, but do not
prove the adequacy of, a logarithmic transformation.

```{r sales-distribution-and-transformation, echo=FALSE, results='hide', fig.height=6.4}
stopifnot(all(na.omit(daily_sales$sales) >= 0))
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
hist(daily_sales$sales, breaks = 45, col = "grey80", main = "Distribution of Daily Total Sales", xlab = "Sales (units)")
hist(log1p(daily_sales$sales), breaks = 45, col = "grey80", main = "Distribution of log(1 + Sales)", xlab = "log(1 + daily sales)")
plot(daily_sales$date, log1p(daily_sales$sales), type = "l", main = "Transformed Daily Sales", xlab = "Date", ylab = "log(1 + sales)")
monthly_group <- format(daily_sales$date, "%Y-%m")
monthly_scale <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(daily_sales$sales, monthly_group), function(x) {
  x <- na.omit(x)
  c(mean = mean(x), sd = sd(x), log_sd = sd(log1p(x)))
}))
plot(monthly_scale[, "mean"], monthly_scale[, "sd"], pch = 16,
     main = "Monthly Mean versus Standard Deviation", xlab = "Monthly mean sales", ylab = "Monthly SD sales")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
cat("Correlation of monthly raw mean and SD:", cor(monthly_scale[, "mean"], monthly_scale[, "sd"], use = "complete.obs"), "\n")
```

```{r report-variance-note, results='asis'}
cat(sprintf("The correlation between monthly mean and standard deviation is %.3f. The log1p transformation preserves zero sales and compresses large observations; residual variance is assessed again after fitting.\n\n",
 cor(monthly_scale[, "mean"], monthly_scale[, "sd"], use = "complete.obs")))
```

```{r calendar-grouping, echo=FALSE, results='hide', fig.height=6.2}
complete_daily <- daily_sales[!is.na(daily_sales$sales), ]
complete_daily$weekday <- factor(as.integer(format(complete_daily$date, "%u")),
  levels = 1:7, labels = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"))
complete_daily$month <- as.integer(format(complete_daily$date, "%m"))
complete_daily$year <- format(complete_daily$date, "%Y")
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
boxplot(sales ~ weekday, data = complete_daily, main = "Daily Sales by Weekday", xlab = "Weekday", ylab = "Sales (units)")
boxplot(log1p(sales) ~ weekday, data = complete_daily, main = "Log Sales by Weekday", xlab = "Weekday", ylab = "log(1 + sales)")
month_means <- aggregate(sales ~ month, complete_daily, mean)
year_means <- aggregate(sales ~ year, complete_daily, mean)
barplot(month_means$sales, names.arg = month.abb[month_means$month], main = "Average Daily Sales by Month", ylab = "Mean sales", las = 2)
barplot(year_means$sales, names.arg = year_means$year, main = "Average Daily Sales by Year", ylab = "Mean sales")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
month_year_means <- aggregate(sales ~ year + month, complete_daily, mean)
month_year_counts <- aggregate(sales ~ year + month, complete_daily, length)
stopifnot(identical(month_year_means[c("year", "month")], month_year_counts[c("year", "month")]))
month_year_means$n_days <- month_year_counts$sales
knitr::kable(month_year_means, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

Weekday differences suggest weekly structure, examined with ACF/STL below.
Monthly/yearly averages also mix trend, calendar composition and partial-year
coverage, so they are descriptive rather than separate seasonal-effect estimates.

```{r unusual-days-and-holidays, include=FALSE}
# Tukey fences flag extremes, without declaring them errors or deleting them.
q <- quantile(complete_daily$sales, c(.25, .75))
fences <- q + c(-1.5, 1.5) * diff(q)
flag <- complete_daily$sales < fences[1] | complete_daily$sales > fences[2]
cat("Daily totals outside 1.5-IQR fences:", sum(flag), "; none removed.\n")
# Changes are computed only between adjacent calendar days with observed totals.
daily_sales$change <- c(NA_real_, diff(daily_sales$sales))
daily_sales$percent_change <- c(NA_real_, 100 * diff(daily_sales$sales) / head(daily_sales$sales, -1))
daily_sales$percent_change[!is.finite(daily_sales$percent_change)] <- NA_real_
h <- holidays_events[!is.na(holidays_events$date), ]
holiday_labels <- tapply(paste(h$type, h$locale, h$locale_name, h$description,
                               paste0("transferred=", h$transferred)), h$date,
                         function(x) paste(unique(x), collapse = "; "))
label_days <- function(x) {
  x$holiday_records <- unname(holiday_labels[as.character(x$date)])
  x$weekday <- weekdays(x$date)
  x
}
low_high <- unique(c(head(order(complete_daily$sales), 8), head(order(-complete_daily$sales), 8)))
knitr::kable(label_days(complete_daily[low_high, c("date", "sales")]), row.names = FALSE)
drops <- daily_sales[order(daily_sales$percent_change, na.last = NA), ]
knitr::kable(label_days(head(drops[c("date", "sales", "percent_change")], 12)), digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
boundary <- format(complete_daily$date, "%m-%d") %in% c("12-30", "12-31", "01-01", "01-02", "01-03")
knitr::kable(label_days(complete_daily[boundary, c("date", "sales")]), row.names = FALSE)
# Separate holiday-date summaries by locale; dates may occur in multiple groups.
for (loc in unique(h$locale)) {
  hd <- unique(h$date[h$locale == loc & !is.na(h$transferred) & tolower(as.character(h$transferred)) == "false"])
  z <- complete_daily$sales[complete_daily$date %in% hd]
  cat(loc, "non-transferred event dates: n =", length(z), "; mean sales =", mean(z), "\n")
}
```

```{r report-holiday-extremes, results='asis'}
report_extreme_dates <- unique(c(head(drops$date, 5), complete_daily$date[head(order(-complete_daily$sales), 3)]))
report_events <- daily_sales[match(report_extreme_dates, daily_sales$date), c("date", "sales", "percent_change")]
report_events <- label_days(report_events)
report_events$holiday_records <- ifelse(is.na(report_events$holiday_records), "-",
  paste0(substr(report_events$holiday_records, 1, 58), ifelse(nchar(report_events$holiday_records) > 58, "...", "")))
report_table(report_events, "Largest sales drops and high-sales dates", digits = 1,
 col.names = c("Date", "Sales", "Change (%)", "Event context", "Weekday"), alignment = "llrp{6.2cm}l")
report_years <- sort(unique(format(complete_daily$date, "%Y")))
report_boundaries <- do.call(rbind, lapply(report_years, function(y) {
  jan <- match(as.Date(paste0(y, "-01-01")), daily_sales$date)
  dec <- match(as.Date(paste0(as.integer(y) - 1L, "-12-31")), daily_sales$date)
  data.frame(Year = y, `Previous Dec 31` = daily_sales$sales[dec], `Jan 1` = daily_sales$sales[jan],
    `Jan 1 change (%)` = daily_sales$percent_change[jan], check.names = FALSE)
}))
report_table(report_boundaries, "Year-boundary sales", digits = 1)
cat(sprintf("Daily totals outside the 1.5-IQR fences: %d; **none were removed**. Event descriptions are abbreviated for display.\n\n", sum(flag)))
```

Holiday matches contextualize unusually low/high sales without establishing
causation or confirming errors. Transferred source dates and actual observances
are distinguished in forecasting, and local/regional holidays apply only to
relevant stores. Strong year-boundary drops are retained as genuine observations.

# 3. Trend, weekly seasonality and dependence

For the regular aggregate segment, $z_t=\log(1+y_t)$ is decomposed as
$z_t=T_t+S_t+R_t$ using robust weekly STL (frequency 7; seasonal window 13).
Robust smoothing downweights unusual observations but does not delete them.

```{r aggregate-stl, echo=FALSE, results='hide', fig.keep=1, fig.height=6.2}
y <- ts(segment$value, frequency = 7)
z <- log1p(y)
fit_stl <- stl(z, s.window = 13, robust = TRUE)
plot(fit_stl, main = "Weekly STL of log(1 + Daily Total Sales)")
sa <- z - fit_stl$time.series[, "seasonal"]
trend <- fit_stl$time.series[, "trend"]
seasonal <- fit_stl$time.series[, "seasonal"]
cat("Smoothed trend: first 28-day mean =", mean(head(trend, 28)),
    "; last 28-day mean =", mean(tail(trend, 28)), "\n")
block <- cut(seq_along(seasonal), breaks = 4, labels = FALSE)
seasonal_profiles <- sapply(1:4, function(b) tapply(seasonal[block == b], cycle(z)[block == b], mean))
matplot(1:7, seasonal_profiles, type = "b", pch = 1:4, lty = 1,
  xlab = "Weekly phase (phase 1 = segment start weekday)", ylab = "Log-scale seasonal effect",
  main = "Weekly Seasonal Profiles across Four Time Blocks")
legend("topright", legend = paste("Block", 1:4), col = 1:4, pch = 1:4, lty = 1, bty = "n")
cat("Range of block seasonal amplitudes:", range(apply(seasonal_profiles, 2, function(x) diff(range(x)))), "\n")
```

```{r report-stl-note, results='asis'}
cat(sprintf("The last minus first 28-day mean trend is %.3f log units. Across four time blocks, weekly seasonal amplitudes range from %.3f to %.3f. ",
 mean(tail(trend, 28)) - mean(head(trend, 28)),
 min(apply(seasonal_profiles, 2, function(x) diff(range(x)))),
 max(apply(seasonal_profiles, 2, function(x) diff(range(x))))))
cat("STL shows evolving trend/weekly structure, but does not distinguish deterministic from stochastic trends. Its fitted components are exploratory and are not reused as fixed forecasting regressors.\n\n")
```

```{r dependence-helpers, include=FALSE}
plot_dependence <- function(x, label, lag_max = 56) {
  lag_max <- min(lag_max, floor(length(x) / 4))
  # Numeric input expresses lags in days instead of multiples of frequency 7.
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
  acf(as.numeric(x), lag.max = lag_max, main = paste(label, "ACF"), xlab = "Lag (days)")
  pacf(as.numeric(x), lag.max = lag_max, main = paste(label, "PACF"), xlab = "Lag (days)")
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
}
weekly_acf <- function(x) {
  a <- acf(as.numeric(x), lag.max = 28, plot = FALSE)$acf
  data.frame(lag_days = c(7, 14, 21, 28), acf = as.numeric(a[c(7, 14, 21, 28) + 1]),
             approximate_bound = 1.96 / sqrt(length(x)))
}
```
```{r aggregate-acf-pacf, echo=FALSE, results='hide', fig.height=3.9}
plot_dependence(y, "Original aggregate")
knitr::kable(weekly_acf(y), digits = 4)
plot_dependence(sa, "STL-adjusted log sales")
knitr::kable(weekly_acf(sa), digits = 4)
```

```{r report-weekly-dependence, results='asis'}
report_table(data.frame(`Lag (days)` = c(7,14,21,28), Raw = weekly_acf(y)$acf,
  `Adjusted log` = weekly_acf(sa)$acf, check.names = FALSE), "Weekly-lag autocorrelations", digits = 3)
```

Slow ACF decay is compatible with persistent dependence and changing levels;
weekly-lag correlations complement the weekday plots. The plotted bounds are
pointwise white-noise approximations, not multiplicity-adjusted seasonal tests.
STL adjustment is estimated and itself changes the dependence structure.

# 4. Stationarity and series heterogeneity

ADF tests $H_0$: a unit root. KPSS tests $H_0$: stationarity around the stated
deterministic terms. Raw/log levels include an intercept and trend; differences
use a constant. ADF lag selection allows at least four weeks, and both short and
long KPSS bandwidths are retained to expose sensitivity.

With deterministic terms included, the ADF regression has the form
\[
\Delta z_t=\alpha+\beta t+\gamma z_{t-1}
 +\sum_{j=1}^{p}\psi_j\Delta z_{t-j}+u_t,\qquad H_0:\gamma=0.
\]
The trend term is omitted for the constant-only specification. KPSS instead
tests whether fluctuations around those deterministic terms are stationary;
its long-run variance estimate depends on bandwidth. Short/long decisions
are therefore reported together rather than as repeated independent evidence.

```{r stationarity-test-helpers, include=FALSE}
run_tests <- function(x, label, trend = TRUE) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  stopifnot(!anyNA(x))
  # At least four weeks available for lag selection; Schwert sample-size rule.
  max_lag <- min(max(28L, floor(12 * (length(x) / 100)^.25)), floor(length(x) / 5))
  adf <- urca::ur.df(x, type = if (trend) "trend" else "drift",
                     lags = max_lag, selectlags = "AIC")
  tau <- if (trend) "tau3" else "tau2"
  astat <- as.numeric(adf@teststat[1, tau])
  acrit <- as.numeric(adf@cval[tau, "5pct"])
  # Report both conventional short and long KPSS bandwidth choices.
  rows <- lapply(c("short", "long"), function(bw) {
    kpss <- urca::ur.kpss(x, type = if (trend) "tau" else "mu", lags = bw)
    kstat <- as.numeric(kpss@teststat)
    kcrit <- as.numeric(kpss@cval[1, "5pct"])
    data.frame(series = label, deterministic = if (trend) "intercept + trend" else "intercept",
      n = length(x), ADF_max_lag = max_lag, ADF_lag = sum(grepl("z.diff.lag", rownames(adf@testreg$coefficients), fixed = TRUE)), ADF_stat = astat, ADF_critical_5pct = acrit,
      ADF_reject = astat < acrit, KPSS_bandwidth = bw, KPSS_lag = kpss@lag,
      KPSS_stat = kstat, KPSS_critical_5pct = kcrit, KPSS_reject = kstat > kcrit)
  })
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}
interpret_tests <- function(tab) {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(tab))) {
    r <- tab[i, ]
    cat(r$series, "(", r$KPSS_bandwidth, "KPSS bandwidth): ADF",
        if (r$ADF_reject) "rejects the unit-root null" else "does not reject the unit-root null",
        "; KPSS", if (r$KPSS_reject) "rejects its stationarity null." else "does not reject its stationarity null.", "\n")
  }
}
```
```{r aggregate-stationarity-tests, include=FALSE}
aggregate_tests <- rbind(run_tests(y, "Raw total", TRUE),
                         run_tests(z, "Log total", TRUE),
                         run_tests(sa, "Seasonally adjusted log total", TRUE))
knitr::kable(aggregate_tests, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
interpret_tests(aggregate_tests)
```
```{r first-difference-diagnostics, include=FALSE}
# A diagnostic comparison, not an automatic decision to difference.
dsa <- diff(sa)
plot(segment$date[-1], as.numeric(dsa), type = "l", main = "First Difference of Seasonally Adjusted Log Sales",
     xlab = "Date", ylab = "Change in adjusted log sales")
plot_dependence(dsa, "Differenced adjusted log sales")
difference_tests <- run_tests(dsa, "Differenced adjusted log total", FALSE)
knitr::kable(difference_tests, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
interpret_tests(difference_tests)
```

```{r report-stationarity, results='asis'}
report_stationarity(rbind(aggregate_tests, difference_tests), "Aggregate stationarity results")
```

Rejecting ADF is evidence against a unit root; non-rejection is not proof of one.
Disagreement with KPSS leaves uncertainty rather than proving stationarity.
A deterministic-trend interpretation has mean-reverting shocks around a fixed
trend; a stochastic trend permits persistent level shocks. First differences are
a diagnostic alternative, not an automatic response to an increasing plot.
Over-differencing can introduce negative short-lag correlation. Weekly
seasonality alone does not require seasonal differencing.

```{r report-differenced-plots, fig.height=3.9}
plot(segment$date[-1], as.numeric(dsa), type = "l", main = "Differenced adjusted log sales",
 xlab = "Date", ylab = "Change in adjusted log sales")
plot_dependence(dsa, "Differenced adjusted log sales")
```

```{r individual-series-diagnostics, include=FALSE}
report_individual_details <- list()
individual_tests <- list()
individual_features <- list()
for (j in seq_len(nrow(chosen))) {
  key <- chosen$key[j]
  x <- t[series_rows[[key]], c("date", "sales")]
  x <- merge(calendar, x, by = "date", all.x = TRUE, sort = TRUE)
  s <- longest_segment(x$date, x$sales)
  cat("\nSeries:", key, "; absent or missing sales dates:", sum(is.na(x$sales)),
      "; contiguous segment:", as.character(min(s$date)), "to", as.character(max(s$date)),
      "; n =", length(s$value), "; dates outside segment:", s$omitted, "\n")
  plot(x$date, x$sales, type = "l", main = paste("Sales:", key), xlab = "Date", ylab = "Sales (units)")
  if (length(s$value) < 60 || var(s$value) == 0) {
    cat("Insufficient length or variation for these diagnostics.\n")
    next
  }
  stopifnot(all(s$value >= 0))
  zi <- ts(log1p(s$value), frequency = 7)
  fi <- stl(zi, s.window = 13, robust = TRUE)
  plot(fi, main = paste("Weekly Log-Sales STL:", key))
  sai <- zi - fi$time.series[, "seasonal"]
  report_individual_details[[key]] <- list(x = x, s = s, zi = zi, fi = fi, sai = sai)
  plot_dependence(zi, paste(key, "log sales"))
  plot_dependence(sai, paste(key, "adjusted"))
  ti <- rbind(run_tests(zi, paste(key, "log"), TRUE),
              run_tests(sai, paste(key, "adjusted"), TRUE))
  print(knitr::kable(ti, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE))
  interpret_tests(ti)
  individual_tests[[key]] <- ti
  remainder <- fi$time.series[, "remainder"]
  individual_features[[key]] <- data.frame(series = key, n = length(zi),
    zero_fraction = mean(s$value == 0),
    trend_endpoint_change = mean(tail(fi$time.series[, "trend"], 28)) - mean(head(fi$time.series[, "trend"], 28)),
    seasonal_strength = max(0, 1 - var(remainder) / var(remainder + fi$time.series[, "seasonal"])),
    log_ACF7 = weekly_acf(zi)$acf[1], adjusted_ACF7 = weekly_acf(sai)$acf[1])
}
features <- do.call(rbind, individual_features)
knitr::kable(features, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r report-individual-comparison, results='asis'}
 KPSS = paste(report_individual[["KPSS log"]], report_individual[["KPSS adjusted"]], sep = "; "))
report_table(report_individual_compact, "Three-series EDA-segment comparison", digits = 3,
 col.names = c("Series", "Zero %", "Trend", "Strength", "ADF log/adj", "KPSS log; adj"), alignment = "p{3.8cm}rrrrl")
cat("ADF gives log/adjusted decisions; each KPSS pair gives short/long bandwidth decisions, first log then adjusted. R = reject; NR = do not reject.\n\n")

```

The detailed plots show one example; all three are analyzed in the source.
Trend change is the endpoint difference in 28-day mean STL trend on log scale.
All comparison metrics refer to their complete EDA segments. Seasonal strength is
$F_S=\max\{0,1-\operatorname{Var}(R_t)/\operatorname{Var}(S_t+R_t)\}$,
a descriptive variance ratio rather than a hypothesis test.
Variation in these measures, zeros and stationarity decisions demonstrates why
aggregate findings cannot be imposed on every store-family series. All regular
EDA diagnostics use their complete contiguous segment; final model fitting uses
the full history, not just the 365-observation exploratory segment.

# 5. Forecasting features

Write $Z_t=\log(1+Y_t)$. The regression features are linear time trend, weekday
indicators, $\log(1+\mathrm{onpromotion})$, localized holiday/compensating-workday
flags, payday indicators for the 15th/month end, and annual Fourier terms
\[
S_t=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\{a_k\sin(2\pi kt/365.25)+b_k\cos(2\pi kt/365.25)\},
\qquad K\in\{1,2,3\}.
\]
Month ends include February/leap years. National events apply to all stores;
regional/local events match state/city. Transferred source holidays are excluded
and destination observances included. Binary event flags avoid duplicate joins.
Unplanned events and unknown future transactions/oil prices are excluded. Store
attributes are constant within a series and would duplicate its intercept.

Full-history OLS BIC/AICc screens $K=1,2,3$. Their IID-error criteria are only
screening proxies. The final comparison uses joint exact likelihood, comparing
$K=1$ with the better higher-order screen at the winning error order. QR checks
remove constants/aliases, including after differencing. Training and future
matrices have identical columns and categorical encodings.

```{r modeling-configuration, include=FALSE}
# All model definitions are embedded below: no external R script required.
# Classical store-family forecasting. No packages are attached to the search path.
if (!requireNamespace("forecast", quietly = TRUE)) stop("Install package 'forecast'.")
row_key <- function(x) paste(x$date, x$store_nbr, x$family, sep = "|")
pair_key <- function(x) paste(x$store_nbr, x$family, sep = " | ")

make_holiday_calendar <- function(stores, events, dates) {
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(stores$store_nbr))
  out <- expand.grid(date = dates, store_nbr = stores$store_nbr)
  out$date <- as.Date(out$date, origin = "1970-01-01")
  out$holiday <- 0L; out$workday <- 0L
  # Source dates marked transferred are not observances; Transfer rows supply
  # destination dates. Additional/Bridge days count as observances, Work Day
  # compensating dates get a separate flag. Event rows are not called holidays.
  eligible <- !is.na(events$transferred) &
    tolower(as.character(events$transferred)) == "false"
  e <- events[eligible & events$type %in%
    c("Holiday", "Transfer", "Additional", "Bridge", "Work Day"), ]
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(e))) {
    st <- switch(e$locale[i], National = stores$store_nbr,
      Regional = stores$store_nbr[stores$state == e$locale_name[i]],
      Local = stores$store_nbr[stores$city == e$locale_name[i]], integer())
    ix <- out$date == e$date[i] & out$store_nbr %in% st
    field <- if (e$type[i] == "Work Day") "workday" else "holiday"
    out[[field]][ix] <- 1L
  }
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(paste(out$date, out$store_nbr)))
  out
}

make_features <- function(date, promotion, holiday, workday) {
  time <- as.numeric(date - as.Date("2013-01-01"))
  x <- data.frame(trend = time / 365.25,
    weekday = factor((as.integer(date) + 3L) %% 7L + 1L, levels = 1:7),
    promo = log1p(promotion), holiday = holiday, workday = workday,
    payday15 = as.integer(format(date, "%d") == "15"),
    payday_end = as.integer(format(date + 1L, "%m") != format(date, "%m")))
  for (k in 1:3) {
    suffix <- if (k == 1L) "" else as.character(k)
    x[[paste0("annual_sin", suffix)]] <- sin(2 * pi * k * time / 365.25)
    x[[paste0("annual_cos", suffix)]] <- cos(2 * pi * k * time / 365.25)
  }
  x
}

prepare_series <- function(history, future, holiday_calendar) {
  stopifnot(length(unique(history$store_nbr)) == 1L,
    length(unique(history$family)) == 1L, !anyDuplicated(history$date),
    !anyDuplicated(future$date), all(history$date < min(future$date)))
  a <- data.frame(date = seq(as.Date("2013-01-01"), min(future$date) - 1L, by = "day"))
  ix <- match(a$date, history$date)
  a$sales <- history$sales[ix]; a$onpromotion <- history$onpromotion[ix]
  b <- future[order(future$date), , drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(all(diff(as.numeric(a$date)) == 1), all(diff(as.numeric(b$date)) == 1),
            min(b$date) == max(a$date) + 1)
  sid <- as.character(history$store_nbr[1])
  hd <- if (is.data.frame(holiday_calendar)) {
    list(data = holiday_calendar[holiday_calendar$store_nbr == as.integer(sid), ], features = NULL)
  } else holiday_calendar[[sid]]
  ia <- match(a$date, hd$data$date); ib <- match(b$date, hd$data$date)
  stopifnot(!anyNA(ia), !anyNA(ib))
  med <- median(a$onpromotion, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(med)) med <- 0
  npa <- sum(is.na(a$onpromotion)); npb <- sum(is.na(b$onpromotion))
  # Impute covariates only, using this series' training median. Never fill sales.
  a$onpromotion[is.na(a$onpromotion)] <- med
  b$onpromotion[is.na(b$onpromotion)] <- med
  if (is.null(hd$features)) {
    xa <- make_features(a$date, a$onpromotion, hd$data$holiday[ia], hd$data$workday[ia])
    xb <- make_features(b$date, b$onpromotion, hd$data$holiday[ib], hd$data$workday[ib])
  } else {
    xa <- hd$features[ia, , drop = FALSE]; xb <- hd$features[ib, , drop = FALSE]
    xa$promo <- log1p(a$onpromotion); xb$promo <- log1p(b$onpromotion)
  }
  stopifnot(!anyNA(xa), !anyNA(xb), all(a$sales[!is.na(a$sales)] >= 0))
  list(history = a, future = b, xa = xa, xb = xb,
    missing_sales = sum(is.na(a$sales)), absent_dates = sum(is.na(ix)),
    missing_promo_train = npa, missing_promo_future = npb)
}

xreg_pair <- function(prep, extended = TRUE, integrated = FALSE, seasonal_difference = FALSE, K = 1L) {
  stopifnot(K %in% 1:3)
  suffix <- c("", if (K >= 2L) as.character(2:K))
  annual <- as.vector(rbind(paste0("annual_sin", suffix), paste0("annual_cos", suffix)))
  terms <- c(if (!integrated) "trend", if (!seasonal_difference) "weekday", "promo",
             "payday15", "payday_end", if (extended) c("holiday", "workday", annual))
  f <- reformulate(terms)
  a <- model.matrix(f, prep$xa); b <- model.matrix(f, prep$xb)
  stopifnot(identical(colnames(a), colnames(b)))
  # Remove constants and then aliases relative to the model intercept, using
  # training observations only. Intercept is fitted by lm/Arima, not duplicated.
  observed <- !is.na(prep$history$sales)
  keep <- colnames(a) != "(Intercept)" & apply(a[observed, , drop = FALSE], 2, function(x) diff(range(x)) > 1e-10)
  a <- a[, keep, drop = FALSE]; b <- b[, keep, drop = FALSE]
  augmented <- cbind(intercept = 1, a[observed, , drop = FALSE])
  q <- qr(augmented)
  good <- sort(q$pivot[seq_len(q$rank)])
  cols <- setdiff(colnames(augmented)[good], "intercept")
  dropped <- setdiff(colnames(a), cols)
  a <- a[, cols, drop = FALSE]; b <- b[, cols, drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(identical(colnames(a), colnames(b)), !anyNA(a), !anyNA(b),
    qr(cbind(1, a[observed, , drop = FALSE]))$rank == ncol(a) + 1)
  list(train = a, future = b, dropped = dropped)
}

seasonal_naive <- function(prep) {
  a <- prep$history; b <- prep$future
  weekday <- (as.integer(a$date) + 3L) %% 7L + 1L
  observed <- a$sales[!is.na(a$sales)]
  last <- if (length(observed)) tail(observed, 1L) else 0
  by_weekday <- rep(last, 7L)
  for (day in 1:7) {
    values <- a$sales[!is.na(a$sales) & weekday == day]
    if (length(values)) by_weekday[day] <- tail(values, 1L)
  }
  unname(by_weekday[(as.integer(b$date) + 3L) %% 7L + 1L])
}

regular_tail <- function(x) {
  r <- rle(!is.na(x)); ends <- cumsum(r$lengths)
  j <- which(r$values)
  if (!length(j)) return(numeric())
  k <- tail(j, 1)
  x[seq.int(ends[k] - r$lengths[k] + 1L, ends[k])]
}

identify_differences <- function(z, adjusted = NULL) {
  # Only diagnostics use contiguous segments; all joint ML fits retain all dates.
  if (is.null(adjusted)) {
    tt <- seq_along(z); dow <- factor((tt - 1L) %% 7L, levels = 0:6)
    xx <- model.matrix(~ tt + dow); ok <- !is.na(z)
    adjusted <- rep(NA_real_, length(z))
    if (sum(ok) > ncol(xx)) adjusted[ok] <- lm.fit(xx[ok, , drop = FALSE], z[ok])$residuals
  }
  s <- regular_tail(z); r <- regular_tail(adjusted); issues <- character()
  defaults <- list(d = 0L, D = 0L, n = min(length(s), length(r)), seas = NA, ocsb = NA,
    raw_level_kpss = NA, raw_trend_kpss = NA, raw_trend_adf = NA, adjusted_kpss = NA,
    raw_acf7 = NA_real_, adjusted_acf7 = NA_real_, difference_acf1 = NA_real_,
    weekly_difference_acf7 = NA_real_, issue = "",
    justification = "Insufficient regular diagnostic segment/variation: conservative d=D=0")
  if (length(s) < 80L || length(r) != length(s) || var(r) < 1e-12) return(defaults)
  safe <- function(expr, label) tryCatch(withCallingHandlers(expr,
    warning = function(w) {
      issues <<- c(issues, paste(label, conditionMessage(w))); invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }), error = function(e) {
      issues <<- c(issues, paste(label, conditionMessage(e), "support defaulted to 0")); 0L
    })
  s <- ts(s, frequency = 7); r <- ts(r, frequency = 7)
  get_acf <- function(x, lag) as.numeric(acf(as.numeric(x), lag.max = lag, plot = FALSE)$acf[lag + 1L])
  seas <- safe(forecast::nsdiffs(r, test = "seas", max.D = 1), "Adjusted seasonal strength:")
  ocsb <- safe(forecast::nsdiffs(r, test = "ocsb", max.D = 1), "Adjusted OCSB:")
  ac7 <- get_acf(r, 7L)
  D <- as.integer(seas == 1L && ocsb == 1L && ac7 > 1.96 / sqrt(length(r)))
  w <- if (D) diff(s, lag = 7) else s
  v <- if (D) diff(r, lag = 7) else r
  raw_level <- safe(forecast::ndiffs(w, test = "kpss", type = "level", max.d = 1), "Raw level KPSS:")
  type <- if (D) "level" else "trend"
  raw_trend <- safe(forecast::ndiffs(w, test = "kpss", type = type, max.d = 1), "Raw deterministic-specification KPSS:")
  raw_adf <- safe(forecast::ndiffs(w, test = "adf", type = type, max.d = 1), "Raw deterministic-specification ADF:")
  adjusted_kpss <- safe(forecast::ndiffs(v, test = "kpss", type = "level", max.d = 1), "Adjusted-component KPSS screen:")
  # Conservative evidence agreement, not proof. ADF inference is on the raw
  # series with explicit deterministic terms, never on fitted OLS residuals.
  d <- as.integer(raw_trend == 1L && raw_adf == 1L && adjusted_kpss == 1L)
  reason <- if (d) "Raw deterministic-specification ADF/KPSS and adjusted-component screen support d=1" else
    "Evidence does not jointly require d=1; retain deterministic trend with stationary errors"
  if (raw_trend != raw_adf) issues <- c(issues, "ADF/KPSS support disagrees; no definitive unit-root conclusion")
  if (D) reason <- paste(reason, "; D=1 supported after removing deterministic calendar effects") else
    reason <- paste(reason, "; deterministic weekday effects retained, D=0")
  list(d = d, D = D, n = length(s), seas = seas, ocsb = ocsb,
    raw_level_kpss = raw_level, raw_trend_kpss = raw_trend, raw_trend_adf = raw_adf,
    adjusted_kpss = adjusted_kpss, raw_acf7 = get_acf(s, 7L), adjusted_acf7 = ac7,
    difference_acf1 = get_acf(diff(w), 1L), weekly_difference_acf7 = get_acf(diff(r, lag = 7), 7L),
    issue = paste(unique(issues), collapse = "; "), justification = reason)
}

root_check <- function(fit) {
  roots <- function(v, sign) {
    if (!length(v) || all(abs(v) < 1e-12)) return(Inf)
    min(Mod(polyroot(c(1, sign * v))))
  }
  c(AR_root = roots(fit$model$phi, -1), MA_root = roots(fit$model$theta, 1))
}

screen_fourier <- function(prep, z) {
  ok <- !is.na(z); n <- sum(ok)
  rows <- list(); residuals <- list()
  for (K in 1:3) {
    xr <- xreg_pair(prep, extended = TRUE, K = K)
    f <- lm.fit(cbind(intercept = 1, xr$train[ok, , drop = FALSE]), z[ok])
    k <- f$rank + 1L  # regression coefficients plus innovation variance
    rss <- max(sum(f$residuals^2), .Machine$double.eps)
    rows[[K]] <- data.frame(K = K, n = n, parameters = k,
      iid_AICc_screen = n * log(rss / n) + 2 * k + 2 * k * (k + 1) / (n - k - 1),
      iid_BIC_screen = n * log(rss / n) + log(n) * k)
    e <- rep(NA_real_, length(z)); e[ok] <- f$residuals; residuals[[K]] <- e
  }
  tab <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  seed <- tab$K[which.min(tab$iid_BIC_screen)]
  higher <- tab$K[tab$K > 1L][which.min(tab$iid_BIC_screen[tab$K > 1L])]
  # Always compare the parsimonious K=1 with the better higher-order screen.
  shortlist <- unique(c(seed, 1L, higher))
  tab$shortlisted <- tab$K %in% shortlist
  list(table = tab, seed = seed, shortlist = shortlist, residual = residuals[[seed]])
}

screen_orders <- function(z, d, D, adjusted = NULL) {
  r <- regular_tail(if (is.null(adjusted)) z else adjusted)
  issues <- character(); pilot <- NULL
  if (length(r) >= 80L && is.finite(var(r)) && var(r) > 1e-12) {
    pilot <- tryCatch(withCallingHandlers(
      forecast::auto.arima(ts(r, frequency = 7), d = d, D = D,
        max.p = 2, max.q = 2, max.P = 1, max.Q = 1,
        start.p = 1, start.q = 1, start.P = 0, start.Q = 0,
        stepwise = TRUE, nmodels = 18, approximation = TRUE,
        allowmean = FALSE, allowdrift = FALSE, parallel = FALSE),
      warning = function(w) { issues <<- c(issues, conditionMessage(w)); invokeRestart("muffleWarning") }),
      error = function(e) { issues <<- c(issues, conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
  }
  if (!is.null(pilot) && isTRUE(pilot$code == 0)) {
    first <- as.integer(pilot$arma[1:4])  # compact p,q,P,Q always includes zero seasonal orders
  } else first <- c(0L, 1L, 0L, 1L)
  reference <- c(0L, 1L, 0L, 1L)
  lag_values <- function(x, partial = FALSE) {
    a <- if (partial) pacf(x, lag.max = 2, plot = FALSE)$acf else acf(x, lag.max = 2, plot = FALSE)$acf[-1]
    as.numeric(a)
  }
  list(specs = list(first, c(1L, 0L, 1L, 0L), reference, c(1L, 1L, 0L, 1L)), pilot = pilot, n = length(r),
    acf2 = if (length(r) > 10L && var(r) > 0) lag_values(r) else c(0, 0),
    pacf2 = if (length(r) > 10L && var(r) > 0) lag_values(r, TRUE) else c(0, 0),
    issue = paste(unique(issues), collapse = "; "))
}

fit_arima_candidates <- function(z, xreg = NULL, d = 0L, D = 0L,
                                 specs = NULL, K = 1L, warm_fit = NULL) {
  if (is.null(specs)) specs <- screen_orders(z, d, D)$specs
  id <- vapply(specs, paste, collapse = ",", "")
  specs <- specs[!duplicated(id)]
  fits <- vector("list", length(specs)); rows <- vector("list", length(specs))
  y <- ts(z, frequency = 7)
  if (!is.null(xreg) && !ncol(xreg)) xreg <- NULL
  mean_term <- d + D == 0L
  drift_term <- is.null(xreg) && d == 1L && D == 0L
  for (i in seq_along(specs)) {
    s <- as.integer(specs[[i]])
    stopifnot(length(s) == 4L, all(s >= 0L), all(s[1:2] <= 2L), all(s[3:4] <= 1L))
    warnings <- character(); errors <- character(); attempts <- 0L; failed_calls <- 0L
    start <- proc.time()[3]; initial <- NULL
    prior <- if (i > 1L && !is.null(fits[[i - 1L]])) fits[[i - 1L]] else warm_fit
    if (!is.null(prior) && isTRUE(prior$code == 0)) {
      names_arma <- c(if (s[1]) paste0("ar", seq_len(s[1])), if (s[2]) paste0("ma", seq_len(s[2])),
                      if (s[3]) paste0("sar", seq_len(s[3])), if (s[4]) paste0("sma", seq_len(s[4])))
      v <- setNames(rep(0, length(names_arma)), names_arma)
      common <- intersect(names_arma, names(coef(prior))); v[common] <- coef(prior)[common]
      # NA regression starts are initialized in R's internal orthogonal basis.
      initial <- c(unname(v), rep(NA_real_, if (is.null(xreg)) 0L else ncol(xreg)),
                   if (mean_term || drift_term) NA_real_)
    }
    estimate <- function(init = NULL, maxit = 250L) {
      attempts <<- attempts + 1L
      f <- tryCatch(withCallingHandlers(
        forecast::Arima(y, order = c(s[1], d, s[2]),
          seasonal = list(order = c(s[3], D, s[4]), period = 7),
          xreg = xreg, include.mean = mean_term, include.drift = drift_term,
          method = "ML", init = init, optim.control = list(maxit = maxit)),
        warning = function(w) { warnings <<- c(warnings, conditionMessage(w)); invokeRestart("muffleWarning") }),
        error = function(e) { errors <<- c(errors, conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
      if (is.null(f) || !isTRUE(f$code == 0)) failed_calls <<- failed_calls + 1L
      f
    }
    f <- estimate(initial)
    if ((!is.null(initial) && (is.null(f) || !isTRUE(f$code == 0))) ||
        (!is.null(f) && isTRUE(f$code == 1))) f <- estimate(NULL, 500L)
    roots <- tryCatch(if (!is.null(f)) root_check(f) else c(AR_root = NA_real_, MA_root = NA_real_),
      error = function(e) { errors <<- c(errors, conditionMessage(e)); c(AR_root = NA_real_, MA_root = NA_real_) })
    valid <- !is.null(f) && isTRUE(f$code == 0) && all(is.finite(coef(f))) &&
      is.finite(f$sigma2) && f$sigma2 > 0 && is.finite(f$aicc) &&
      all(is.finite(diag(f$var.coef))) && all(diag(f$var.coef) > 0) &&
      all(!is.na(roots) & roots > 1 + 1e-6)
    rows[[i]] <- data.frame(candidate = i, K = K,
      p = s[1], q = s[2], P = s[3], Qseasonal = s[4],
      order = sprintf("(%d,%d,%d)(%d,%d,%d)[7]", s[1], d, s[2], s[3], D, s[4]),
      AICc = if (!is.null(f)) f$aicc else NA_real_, BIC = if (!is.null(f)) f$bic else NA_real_,
      AR_root = roots[1], MA_root = roots[2], convergence = if (!is.null(f)) f$code else NA_integer_,
      valid = valid, attempts = attempts, failed_calls = failed_calls,
      seconds = unname(proc.time()[3] - start), warning = paste(unique(warnings), collapse = "; "),
      error = paste(unique(errors), collapse = "; "), row.names = NULL)
    fits[i] <- list(f)
  }
  tab <- do.call(rbind, rows); good <- which(tab$valid)
  ranked <- good[order(tab$AICc[good], tab$K[good], good)]
  list(fit = if (length(ranked)) fits[[ranked[1]]] else NULL,
       fits = fits, table = tab, ranked = ranked)
}

innovation_diagnostics <- function(residual, fitdf = 0L) {
  e <- regular_tail(as.numeric(residual))
  # Do not remove internal NAs and collapse time. Diagnostic segment length reported.
  if (length(e) < 40 || !is.finite(var(e)) || var(e) < 1e-12) return(data.frame())
  out <- lapply(c(14L, 28L), function(h) {
    h <- min(h, floor(length(e) / 5))
    if (h <= fitdf) return(NULL)
    b <- Box.test(e, lag = h, type = "Ljung-Box", fitdf = fitdf)
    data.frame(n = length(e), mean = mean(e), lag = h, Q = unname(b$statistic),
      df = unname(b$parameter), p_value = b$p.value, reject_5pct = b$p.value < .05,
      variance_first_half = var(head(e, floor(length(e) / 2))),
      variance_second_half = var(tail(e, floor(length(e) / 2))))
  })
  do.call(rbind, out)
}

# Estimate one primary regression model family, rather than M2/M3/M3_base
# repeatedly. Only the illustrative example receives separate benchmark fits.
prepare_regression <- function(prep, d, D, extended = TRUE, K = 1L) {
  xr <- xreg_pair(prep, extended = extended, integrated = d + D > 0L, seasonal_difference = D > 0L, K = K)
  if (d + D > 0L && ncol(xr$train)) {
    xd <- xr$train
    if (D) xd <- diff(xd, lag = 7)
    if (d) xd <- diff(xd)
    q <- qr(xd); good <- if (q$rank) sort(q$pivot[seq_len(q$rank)]) else integer()
    xr$train <- xr$train[, good, drop = FALSE]; xr$future <- xr$future[, good, drop = FALSE]
    stopifnot(qr(xd[, good, drop = FALSE])$rank == ncol(xr$train))
  }
  stopifnot(identical(colnames(xr$train), colnames(xr$future)))
  xr
}

fallback_prediction <- function(prep, sparse = FALSE) {
  y <- prep$history$sales; dates <- prep$history$date
  if (!sparse) return(seasonal_naive(prep))
  weekday <- (as.integer(dates) + 3L) %% 7L + 1L
  z <- log1p(y); ok <- !is.na(z)
  overall <- if (any(ok)) mean(z[ok]) else 0
  level <- vapply(1:7, function(d) if (any(ok & weekday == d)) mean(z[ok & weekday == d]) else overall, numeric(1))
  pmax(0, expm1(level[(as.integer(prep$future$date) + 3L) %% 7L + 1L]))
}

fit_primary <- function(prep, keep_fit = FALSE) {
  start <- proc.time()[3]
  y <- prep$history$sales; z <- log1p(y); observed <- y[!is.na(y)]
  zero_fraction <- if (length(observed)) mean(observed == 0) else NA_real_
  recent <- tail(y, 91L)
  inactive <- length(observed) >= 365L && any(observed > 0) && zero_fraction >= .9 &&
    length(recent) == 91L && !anyNA(recent) && all(recent == 0) &&
    prep$missing_promo_future == 0L && all(prep$future$onpromotion == 0)
  planned <- if (!length(observed)) "M0_no_history" else if (all(observed == 0)) "M0_all_zero" else
    if (inactive) "M0_recent_inactive" else if (length(unique(observed)) == 1L) "M0_constant" else
    if (length(observed) < 60L) "M0_short_history" else ""
  sparse <- is.finite(zero_fraction) && zero_fraction >= .8
  fallback <- if (planned %in% c("M0_no_history", "M0_all_zero", "M0_recent_inactive"))
    rep(0, nrow(prep$future)) else fallback_prediction(prep, sparse = sparse && !nzchar(planned))
  selected <- if (nzchar(planned)) planned else if (sparse) "M0_smoothed_weekday" else "M0_seasonal_naive"
  selected_K <- 0L; f <- NULL; selected_xr <- NULL; candidates <- data.frame()
  diag <- data.frame(); reason <- if (nzchar(planned)) planned else ""; notes <- character()
  fourier_table <- data.frame(); identification <- NULL; order_screen <- NULL
  dif <- list(d = 0L, D = 0L, n = length(regular_tail(z)), seas = NA, ocsb = NA, issue = "",
    justification = "Planned historical-information fallback; unit-root selection not needed",
    raw_level_kpss = NA, raw_trend_kpss = NA, raw_trend_adf = NA, adjusted_kpss = NA,
    raw_acf7 = NA_real_, adjusted_acf7 = NA_real_, difference_acf1 = NA_real_, weekly_difference_acf7 = NA_real_)
  prediction <- fallback
  if (!nzchar(planned)) prediction <- tryCatch(withCallingHandlers({
    fs <- screen_fourier(prep, z); fourier_table <- fs$table
    dif <- identify_differences(z, fs$residual)
    identification <- dif
    os <- screen_orders(z, dif$d, dif$D, adjusted = fs$residual); order_screen <- os
    notes <- c(notes, os$issue)
    xr_by_K <- list(); model_fits <- list()
    seed_K <- fs$seed
    xr_by_K[[as.character(seed_K)]] <- prepare_regression(prep, dif$d, dif$D, K = seed_K)
    cf <- fit_arima_candidates(z, xr_by_K[[as.character(seed_K)]]$train,
      dif$d, dif$D, specs = os$specs, K = seed_K, warm_fit = os$pilot)
    candidates <- cf$table; model_fits <- cf$fits
    ranked <- function() {
      good <- which(candidates$valid)
      good[order(candidates$AICc[good], candidates$K[good], good)]
    }
    good <- ranked()
    if (!length(good) && seed_K != 1L) {
      # A complicated Fourier screen must not force a fallback when the
      # parsimonious K=1 regression can still be estimated reliably.
      xr_by_K[["1"]] <- prepare_regression(prep, dif$d, dif$D, K = 1L)
      rescue <- fit_arima_candidates(z, xr_by_K[["1"]]$train, dif$d, dif$D,
        specs = list(c(0L, 1L, 0L, 1L), c(1L, 0L, 1L, 0L)), K = 1L)
      candidates <- rbind(candidates, rescue$table); model_fits <- c(model_fits, rescue$fits)
      good <- ranked()
    }
    if (!length(good)) stop("No valid joint candidate in the primary order search")
    winner <- good[1]
    # Coordinate search: hold the winning ARMA order and d,D fixed while
    # comparing the second Fourier K by the same full-data exact likelihood.
    alt_K <- setdiff(fs$shortlist, unique(candidates$K))
    for (K in alt_K) {
      xr_by_K[[as.character(K)]] <- prepare_regression(prep, dif$d, dif$D, K = K)
      s <- as.integer(unlist(candidates[winner, c("p", "q", "P", "Qseasonal")], use.names = FALSE))
      alt <- fit_arima_candidates(z, xr_by_K[[as.character(K)]]$train,
        dif$d, dif$D, specs = list(s), K = K, warm_fit = model_fits[[winner]])
      candidates <- rbind(candidates, alt$table); model_fits <- c(model_fits, alt$fits)
    }
    good <- ranked(); winner <- good[1]
    initial_diag <- innovation_diagnostics(residuals(model_fits[[winner]]),
      sum(model_fits[[winner]]$arma[c(1, 2, 3, 4)]))
    # One targeted neighbor only when both weekly-relevant diagnostic lags reject.
    # The cap is six distinct joint candidates, excluding convergence retries.
    if (nrow(candidates) < 6L && nrow(initial_diag) == 2L && all(initial_diag$reject_5pct)) {
      s <- as.integer(unlist(candidates[winner, c("p", "q", "P", "Qseasonal")], use.names = FALSE))
      dimension <- if (abs(os$pacf2[2]) > abs(os$acf2[2])) 1L else 2L
      possibilities <- list()
      for (j in c(dimension, setdiff(1:2, dimension), 3:4)) {
        v <- s; upper <- if (j <= 2L) 2L else 1L
        v[j] <- if (v[j] < upper) v[j] + 1L else max(0L, v[j] - 1L)
        possibilities[[length(possibilities) + 1L]] <- v
      }
      K <- candidates$K[winner]
      existing <- apply(candidates[candidates$K == K, c("p", "q", "P", "Qseasonal"), drop = FALSE], 1, paste, collapse = ",")
      unused <- which(!vapply(possibilities, paste, collapse = ",", "") %in% existing)
      if (length(unused)) {
        extra <- fit_arima_candidates(z, xr_by_K[[as.character(K)]]$train, dif$d, dif$D,
          specs = possibilities[unused[1]], K = K, warm_fit = model_fits[[winner]])
        candidates <- rbind(candidates, extra$table); model_fits <- c(model_fits, extra$fits)
      }
    }
    stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(candidates[c("K", "p", "q", "P", "Qseasonal")]))
    candidates$candidate <- seq_len(nrow(candidates))
    p <- NULL
    for (i in ranked()) {
      xr <- xr_by_K[[as.character(candidates$K[i])]]
      possible <- tryCatch({
        ff <- forecast::forecast(model_fits[[i]], h = nrow(prep$future),
          xreg = if (ncol(xr$future)) xr$future else NULL)
        v <- as.numeric(ff$mean)
        if (length(v) != nrow(prep$future) || any(!is.finite(v))) stop("Nonfinite log forecast")
        # Reject numerical overflow, not merely unusual but finite sales levels.
        if (any(v > log(.Machine$double.xmax))) stop("Retransformation would overflow")
        v
      }, error = function(e) { notes <<- c(notes, paste("Forecast candidate", i, conditionMessage(e))); NULL })
      if (!is.null(possible)) {
        f <- model_fits[[i]]; selected_K <- candidates$K[i]; selected_xr <- xr; p <- possible; break
      }
    }
    if (is.null(p)) stop("All valid candidate forecasts failed finiteness/length checks")
    selected <- if (dif$d + dif$D) "M3_integrated" else "M3"
    diag <- innovation_diagnostics(residuals(f), sum(f$arma[c(1, 2, 3, 4)]))
    { out <- pmax(0, expm1(p)); if (any(!is.finite(out))) stop("Invalid retransformed forecast"); out }
  }, warning = function(w) { notes <<- c(notes, conditionMessage(w)); invokeRestart("muffleWarning") }),
  error = function(e) { reason <<- conditionMessage(e); f <<- NULL; selected_K <<- 0L;
    selected <<- if (sparse) "M0_smoothed_weekday" else "M0_seasonal_naive"; diag <<- data.frame(); fallback })
  lb <- function(lag) if (nrow(diag)) diag$p_value[match(lag, diag$lag)] else NA_real_
  roots <- if (!is.null(f)) root_check(f) else c(AR_root = NA_real_, MA_root = NA_real_)
  e <- if (!is.null(f)) regular_tail(as.numeric(residuals(f))) else numeric()
  scale <- if (length(e) > 1L) max(mad(e), sd(e), .Machine$double.eps, na.rm = TRUE) else 1
  extrapolation <- if (length(observed)) max(log1p(prediction)) > max(z, na.rm = TRUE) + 2 * sd(z, na.rm = TRUE) else FALSE
  row <- data.frame(model = selected, K = selected_K,
    AICc = if (!is.null(f)) f$aicc else NA_real_, BIC = if (!is.null(f)) f$bic else NA_real_,
    LjungBox_p14 = lb(14L), LjungBox_p28 = lb(28L), d = dif$d, D = dif$D,
    AR_root = roots[1], MA_root = roots[2],
    observed_training = length(observed), missing_training = prep$missing_sales,
    absent_dates = prep$absent_dates, missing_sales_rows = prep$missing_sales - prep$absent_dates,
    zero_fraction = zero_fraction, recent_inactive = inactive,
    missing_promo_train = prep$missing_promo_train, missing_promo_future = prep$missing_promo_future,
    differencing_segment_n = dif$n, seasonal_strength_recommendation = dif$seas,
    OCSB_recommendation = dif$ocsb, raw_level_KPSS_support = dif$raw_level_kpss,
    raw_trend_KPSS_support = dif$raw_trend_kpss, raw_trend_ADF_support = dif$raw_trend_adf,
    adjusted_KPSS_screen = dif$adjusted_kpss, differencing_reason = dif$justification,
    differencing_issue = dif$issue,
    order_screen_n = if (!is.null(order_screen)) order_screen$n else 0L,
    attempted_candidates = if (nrow(candidates)) paste(paste0("K=", candidates$K, ":", candidates$order), collapse = "; ") else "none",
    ML_calls = if (nrow(candidates)) sum(candidates$attempts) else 0L,
    failed_fit_calls = if (nrow(candidates)) sum(candidates$failed_calls) else 0L,
    successful_candidates = if (nrow(candidates)) sum(candidates$valid) else 0L,
    rejected_candidates = if (nrow(candidates)) sum(!candidates$valid) else 0L,
    order = if (!is.null(f)) paste(forecast::arimaorder(f), collapse = ",") else selected,
    fallback = is.null(f), failure = reason,
    warnings = paste(unique(c(notes[nzchar(notes)], if (nrow(candidates)) candidates$warning[nzchar(candidates$warning)])), collapse = "; "),
    candidate_errors = if (nrow(candidates)) paste(candidates$error[nzchar(candidates$error)], collapse = "; ") else "",
    large_residuals = if (length(e)) sum(abs(e - median(e)) > 6 * scale) else 0L,
    forecast_extrapolation_flag = isTRUE(extrapolation),
    fit_seconds = unname(proc.time()[3] - start), stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
  list(prediction = prediction, row = row, diagnostics = diag, candidates = candidates,
    fourier_screen = fourier_table, identification = identification,
    fit = if (keep_fit) f else NULL, xr = if (keep_fit) selected_xr else NULL)
}

forecast_job <- function(key, context) {
  h <- context$train[context$hi[[key]], , drop = FALSE]
  f <- context$test[context$ti[[key]], , drop = FALSE]
  h <- h[order(h$date), , drop = FALSE]; f <- f[order(f$date), , drop = FALSE]
  keep <- key %in% context$detail_keys
  prep <- prepare_series(h, f, context$holidays)
  result <- fit_primary(prep, keep_fit = keep)
  result$row$series <- key
  diag <- result$diagnostics
  if (nrow(diag)) { diag$series <- key; diag$model <- result$row$model }
  list(id = f$id, sales = result$prediction, row = result$row,
    diagnostics = diag,
    candidate_log = if (nrow(result$candidates)) {
      tab <- result$candidates; tab$series <- key; tab
    } else NULL,
    detail = if (keep) list(prep = prep, primary = result, key = key) else NULL)
}

add_example_models <- function(detail) {
  # Report-only fits on ONE example; reuse its primary fit without refitting it.
  prep <- detail$prep; z <- log1p(prep$history$sales); y <- prep$history$sales
  primary <- detail$primary; selected <- primary$row$model
  fits <- list(); candidates <- list(); diagnostics <- list()
  if (selected != "M0") {
    fits[selected] <- list(primary$fit); candidates[[selected]] <- primary$candidates
    diagnostics[[selected]] <- primary$diagnostics
  }
  xr <- xreg_pair(prep, extended = TRUE, K = max(1L, primary$row$K))
  obs <- !is.na(y)
  for (m in c("M1", "M1_raw")) {
    response <- if (m == "M1") z else y
    dd <- data.frame(response = response[obs], xr$train[obs, , drop = FALSE], check.names = FALSE)
    f <- lm(response ~ ., dd, na.action = na.fail)
    fits[[m]] <- f
    e <- rep(NA_real_, length(y)); e[obs] <- residuals(f)
    diagnostics[[m]] <- innovation_diagnostics(e)
  }
  cf <- fit_arima_candidates(z, d = primary$row$d, D = primary$row$D)
  fits["M2"] <- list(cf$fit); candidates[["M2"]] <- cf$table
  if (!is.null(cf$fit)) diagnostics[["M2"]] <- innovation_diagnostics(
    residuals(cf$fit), sum(cf$fit$arma[c(1, 2, 3, 4)]))
  basic <- prepare_regression(prep, primary$row$d, primary$row$D, extended = FALSE)
  if (!ncol(basic$train)) { cb <- cf } else {
    cb <- fit_arima_candidates(z, basic$train, primary$row$d, primary$row$D)
  }
  fits["M3_base"] <- list(cb$fit); candidates[["M3_base"]] <- cb$table
  if (!is.null(cb$fit)) diagnostics[["M3_base"]] <- innovation_diagnostics(
    residuals(cb$fit), sum(cb$fit$arma[c(1, 2, 3, 4)]))
  detail$result <- list(fits = fits, candidates = candidates, diagnostics = diagnostics)
  detail$selected <- selected
  detail
}

final_forecast <- function(train, test, holiday_calendar, workers = 1L, progress_every = 25L) {
  hi <- split(seq_len(nrow(train)), pair_key(train))
  ti <- split(seq_len(nrow(test)), pair_key(test))
  keys <- sort(names(ti)); n <- length(keys)
  stopifnot(all(keys %in% names(hi)), !anyDuplicated(test$id))
  # The detail key is deterministic and needs no preliminary model estimation.
  informative <- vapply(keys, function(k) {
    y <- train$sales[hi[[k]]]; sum(!is.na(y)) >= 60L && length(unique(na.omit(y))) > 1L
  }, TRUE)
  informative_keys <- keys[informative]
  mean_levels <- vapply(informative_keys, function(k) mean(train$sales[hi[[k]]], na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1))
  informative_keys <- informative_keys[order(mean_levels, informative_keys)]
  detail_keys <- if (length(informative_keys)) informative_keys[unique(pmax(1L, round(c(.2, .5, .9) * length(informative_keys))))] else character()
  hd <- split(holiday_calendar, holiday_calendar$store_nbr)
  holidays <- lapply(hd, function(x) list(data = x,
    features = make_features(x$date, rep(0, nrow(x)), x$holiday, x$workday)))
  context <- list(train = train[c("date", "store_nbr", "family", "sales", "onpromotion")],
    test = test[c("date", "store_nbr", "family", "onpromotion", "id")],
    hi = hi, ti = ti, holidays = holidays, detail_keys = detail_keys)
  workers <- as.integer(workers)
  if (length(workers) != 1L || is.na(workers) || workers < 1L) stop("workers must be a positive integer")
  workers <- min(workers, 8L, n)
  cluster <- NULL
  if (workers > 1L) {
    cluster <- tryCatch(parallel::makePSOCKcluster(workers, outfile = ""), error = function(e) {
      warning("PSOCK workers unavailable; running sequentially: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL
    })
    if (!is.null(cluster)) {
      on.exit(parallel::stopCluster(cluster), add = TRUE)
      helpers <- c("make_features", "prepare_series", "xreg_pair", "seasonal_naive", "regular_tail",
        "identify_differences", "root_check", "fit_arima_candidates", "innovation_diagnostics",
        "prepare_regression", "screen_fourier", "screen_orders", "fallback_prediction", "fit_primary", "forecast_job")
      # Rebind exported function environments to worker globals; do not serialize
      # the entire knitting environment or recreate a cluster inside a worker.
      exports <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
      for (name in helpers) {
        fun <- get(name, envir = environment(final_forecast)); environment(fun) <- .GlobalEnv
        assign(name, fun, envir = exports)
      }
      assign("model_context", context, envir = exports)
      parallel::clusterExport(cluster, c(helpers, "model_context"), envir = exports)
      parallel::clusterSetRNGStream(cluster, iseed = 586L)
      parallel::clusterEvalQ(cluster, {
        if (!requireNamespace("forecast", quietly = TRUE)) stop("Worker cannot load forecast")
        forecast_worker <- function(key) forecast_job(key, model_context)
        NULL
      })
    } else workers <- 1L
  }
  ans <- vector("list", n); cumulative <- 0; success <- 0L; fallbacks <- 0L; failed_calls <- 0L; converged <- 0L
  wall_start <- proc.time()[3]
  progress <- list(); progress_every <- max(1L, as.integer(progress_every))
  report <- function(done) {
    wall <- unname(proc.time()[3] - wall_start)
    line <- sprintf("Completed %d/%d | SARIMA series %d | valid candidates %d | fallbacks %d | failed joint attempts %d | fitting %.1f s | elapsed %.1f s | workers %d",
                    done, n, success, converged, fallbacks, failed_calls, cumulative, wall, workers)
    # stderr bypasses knitr's buffered ordinary output for live console progress.
    cat(line, "\n", file = stderr()); flush(stderr())
    progress[[length(progress) + 1L]] <<- data.frame(completed = done, total = n,
      successful_SARIMA_series = success, valid_candidates = converged, fallback_series = fallbacks,
      failed_fit_attempts = failed_calls, cumulative_fitting_seconds = cumulative, wall_seconds = wall, workers = workers)
  }
  report(0L)
  for (first in seq.int(1L, n, by = progress_every)) {
    index <- seq.int(first, min(first + progress_every - 1L, n))
    batch <- if (is.null(cluster)) lapply(keys[index], forecast_job, context = context) else
      parallel::parLapply(cluster, keys[index], "forecast_worker")
    ans[index] <- batch
    cumulative <- cumulative + sum(vapply(batch, function(x) x$row$fit_seconds, numeric(1)))
    success <- success + sum(vapply(batch, function(x) !x$row$fallback, TRUE))
    fallbacks <- fallbacks + sum(vapply(batch, function(x) x$row$fallback, TRUE))
    failed_calls <- failed_calls + sum(vapply(batch, function(x) x$row$failed_fit_calls, numeric(1)))
    converged <- converged + sum(vapply(batch, function(x) x$row$successful_candidates, numeric(1)))
    report(max(index))
  }
  submission <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ans, function(x) data.frame(id = x$id, sales = x$sales)))
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(submission$id), setequal(submission$id, test$id))
  submission <- submission[match(test$id, submission$id), c("id", "sales")]
  rownames(submission) <- NULL
  stopifnot(nrow(submission) == nrow(test), identical(submission$id, test$id),
    !anyNA(submission), all(is.finite(submission$sales)), all(submission$sales >= 0))
  details <- Filter(Negate(is.null), lapply(ans, `[[`, "detail"))
  detail <- if (length(details)) add_example_models(details[[1]]) else NULL
  list(submission = submission, models = do.call(rbind, lapply(ans, `[[`, "row")),
       diagnostics = do.call(rbind, lapply(ans, `[[`, "diagnostics")),
       candidates = do.call(rbind, lapply(ans, `[[`, "candidate_log")),
       progress = do.call(rbind, progress), detail = detail, representative_details = details)
}

stopifnot(max(train$date) == as.Date("2017-08-15"),
          min(test$date) == as.Date("2017-08-16"), max(test$date) == as.Date("2017-08-31"),
          !"sales" %in% names(test), !anyDuplicated(test$id))
# Training key checks were already performed in the EDA; do not repeat them.
stopifnot(duplicate_report$duplicate_key_rows[duplicate_report$dataset == "train"] == 0L,
          duplicate_report$duplicate_key_rows[duplicate_report$dataset == "test"] == 0L)
holiday_calendar <- make_holiday_calendar(stores, holidays_events,
  seq(as.Date("2013-01-01"), max(test$date), by = "day"))
available_cores <- suppressWarnings(parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE))
default_workers <- if (length(available_cores) == 1L && !is.na(available_cores)) min(2L, available_cores) else 1L
workers <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("STORE_SALES_WORKERS", as.character(default_workers)))
cat("Full-history primary regression/SARIMA fitting; requested workers:", workers, "\n")
```

All functions remain inside this R Markdown file and execute when knitted.
Calendar/holiday features are cached per store; calendar matching replaces
repeated merges. Missing targets remain NA. Missing promotions, if any, use that
series' training-only median and are counted. No future sales are imputed or
used in predictors. Known future promotion counts come from `test.csv`.

# 6. Benchmark specifications

The weekly seasonal-naive benchmark repeats the most recent observed training
sale for each future weekday. If a weekday has no observations, it uses the
last observed sale; an entirely unobserved history gives zero. This is a forecast
rule, not zero-filling training data.

OLS benchmarks use the same explanatory variables on log and raw scales:
\[Z_t=\beta_0+\boldsymbol\beta^\top X_t+\varepsilon_t.\]
Their standard errors are nominal when independence/homoskedasticity fail.
Standalone SARIMA uses no external regressors:
\[
\phi(B)\Phi(B^7)(1-B)^d(1-B^7)^D Z_t
=c+\theta(B)\Theta(B^7)a_t.
\]
An intercept is allowed only without differencing; standalone drift is allowed
only for $d=1,D=0$. OLS, standalone SARIMA and core-only regression/SARIMA are
fitted on one illustrative series, not repeatedly across all series. They do
not determine final forecasts through validation or cross-scale AIC comparisons.

# 7. Differencing and SARIMA identification

AR($p$) models theoretically have PACF cutoffs and decaying ACF; MA($q$) models
have ACF cutoffs and decaying PACF. ARMA patterns are typically mixed/decaying.
Seasonal analogues occur at multiples of seven, but empirical patterns are
ambiguous in finite samples.

The unchanged, bounded identification procedure is:

1. Fit preliminary full-history regression to account for deterministic effects.
   Use a complete adjusted segment for diagnostic tests. Select $D=1$ only when
   adjusted seasonal strength and OCSB both support it, with remaining lag-seven
   dependence; otherwise retain weekday effects and $D=0$.
2. Choose $d=1$ only when raw deterministic-specification ADF/KPSS and the adjusted
   KPSS screen jointly support it. Retain the deterministic trend otherwise.
   Disagreements and structural-break caveats are recorded. Fitted-residual
   screens are heuristics; ordinary ADF critical values are not used to claim
   cointegration from OLS residuals.
3. Propose an error order with at most 18 low-dimensional stepwise fits, bounded
   by $0\le p,q\le2$ and $0\le P,Q\le1$. Retain the original anchor orders
   $(p,q,P,Q)=(1,0,1,0),(0,1,0,1),(1,1,0,1)$ and remove duplicates.
4. Refit eligible candidates jointly by exact maximum likelihood on **all
   historical observations**, retaining calendar gaps as NA. Compare Fourier
   dimension at the winning error order. If both lag-14/28 innovation tests
   reject, consider one unused neighboring order guided by short-lag ACF/PACF.
   The cap remains six distinct joint candidates plus logged convergence retries.

For $k$ estimated parameters and $n$ effective observations,
\[
\mathrm{AICc}=-2\ell+2k+\frac{2k(k+1)}{n-k-1},\qquad
\mathrm{BIC}=-2\ell+k\log n.
\]

AICc is the primary penalized-likelihood criterion; BIC supplies a stronger
complexity penalty. Comparisons require the same response data, differencing
and likelihood convention. Approximate screening scores are not presented as
exact joint likelihoods, and this coordinate search is not a global optimum
claim. No model is selected merely because it passes a residual test.

# 8. Regression with SARIMA errors and computation

The primary specification is
\[
Z_t=\beta_0+\boldsymbol\beta^\top X_t+N_t,\qquad
\phi(B)\Phi(B^7)(1-B)^d(1-B^7)^D N_t
=\theta(B)\Theta(B^7)a_t.
\]
Regression coefficients and error parameters are estimated jointly. When
$d+D>0$ the explicit trend is removed; seasonal differencing also removes
weekday dummies. No redundant drift is added. Forecasts cover all 16 future
days without observing intervening sales. Back-transformation is
$\max\{0,\exp(\widehat Z)-1\}$, appropriate to the conditional log-scale target
under RMSLE; it is not claimed to be an unbiased original-scale conditional mean.

Converged fits must have finite coefficients/uncertainty, positive innovation
variance, stationary AR and invertible MA components. Warm starts may reuse
ARMA coefficients, never fixed OLS regression estimates. Failed starts receive
a cold retry; invalid candidates/forecasts are rejected and logged.

Fallbacks remain explicit and unchanged:

- All-zero histories give zero; positive constants give their constant value.
- Recent-inactivity zero forecasts require at least 365 observed days, a past
  positive sale, at least 90% historical zeros, 91 consecutive observed zero days
  at the end, and completely observed zero future promotions. Known future
  promotion activity vetoes this rule; unpromoted reactivation remains a risk.
- Fewer than 60 observations use seasonal naive. If joint fitting fails, use
  seasonal naive or, for at least 80% zeros, a full-history log-weekday mean.

Genuine zeros remain observed, small positive predictions are not rounded to
zero, and unusual observations are not deleted. Finite extrapolations are flagged
rather than capped; overflow/nonfinite predictions cause a fallback.

```{r full-training-and-submission, include=FALSE}
run_start <- proc.time()[3]
final <- final_forecast(train, test, holiday_calendar, workers = workers)
training_seconds <- unname(proc.time()[3] - run_start)
submission <- final$submission
stopifnot(nrow(final$models) == length(unique(pair_key(test))),
          sum(final$models$observed_training) == sum(!is.na(train$sales)))
stopifnot(identical(names(submission), c("id", "sales")),
          nrow(submission) == nrow(test), identical(submission$id, test$id),
          !anyDuplicated(submission$id), all(is.finite(submission$sales)),
          all(submission$sales >= 0))
write.csv(submission, "submission.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("All training dates used. Models fitted for", nrow(final$models), "series.\n")
cat("Elapsed model-fitting seconds:", round(training_seconds, 1), "\n")
cat("Final submission rows:", nrow(submission), "\n")
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(final$models$model)),
             col.names = c("Selected model", "Number of series"), row.names = FALSE)
```
