```{r fitting-progress-summary, include=FALSE}
cat("Total exact ML calls:", sum(final$models$ML_calls), "\n")
cat("Fitting warnings recorded for", sum(nzchar(final$models$warnings)), "series.\n")
```

```{r report-computational-summary, results='asis'}
report_last_progress <- tail(final$progress, 1)
report_table(data.frame(Quantity = c("Series processed", "Successful joint-model series", "Fallback series",
 "Valid model candidates", "Failed fitting attempts (including recovered retries)", "Wall time (minutes)", "Parallel workers"),
 Value = c(format(nrow(final$models), big.mark = ","), format(sum(!final$models$fallback), big.mark = ","),
 format(sum(final$models$fallback), big.mark = ","), format(report_last_progress$valid_candidates, big.mark = ","),
```

Console progress remains active. Parallel execution uses reproducible PSOCK
workers, fixed series order and RNG streams; the default is at most two detected
physical cores, with explicit requests capped at eight. Worker-startup failure
falls back to sequential execution. Cumulative per-series fitting time differs
from wall time under parallel execution.

# 9. Representative model adequacy

For one-step innovations, the Ljung-Box null is
$H_0:\rho_a(1)=\cdots=\rho_a(h)=0$, with
\[
Q=n(n+2)\sum_{k=1}^{h}\frac{\widehat\rho_a(k)^2}{n-k}.
\]
At lags 14/28 the ARIMA reference is approximately
$\chi^2_{h-p-q-P-Q}$. Regression coefficients and differencing are not counted
as ARMA parameters. OLS uses a descriptive `fitdf=0` screen rather than an exact
regression-adjusted test. Failing to reject does not prove white noise; many
series/tests also create multiplicity concerns.

```{r detailed-coefficients-and-diagnostics, include=FALSE}
detail <- final$detail
if (is.null(detail)) cat("All series used fallbacks; no estimable detailed example.\n")
if (!is.null(detail)) {
cat("Detailed full-training example:", detail$key, "\n")
print(knitr::kable(detail$primary$fourier_screen, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Fourier screening proxies; final joint AICc is in the candidate tables"))
for (m in unique(c("M1", "M1_raw", "M2", "M3_base", detail$selected))) {
  f <- detail$result$fits[[m]]
  cat("\nModel", m, "\n")
  if (is.null(f)) { cat("Fallback; no estimated model parameters.\n"); next }
  if (inherits(f, "lm")) {
    print(knitr::kable(coef(summary(f)), digits = 4))
    e <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(detail$prep$history))
    e[!is.na(detail$prep$history$sales)] <- residuals(f)
    fitted_values <- rep(NA_real_, length(e))
    fitted_values[!is.na(detail$prep$history$sales)] <- fitted(f)
  } else {
    se <- sqrt(diag(f$var.coef))
    ct <- data.frame(estimate = coef(f), SE = se, z = coef(f) / se,
      nominal_p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(coef(f) / se)))
    print(knitr::kable(ct, digits = 4))
    print(knitr::kable(detail$result$candidates[[m]], digits = 4, row.names = FALSE))
    e <- as.numeric(residuals(f)); fitted_values <- as.numeric(fitted(f))
  }
  par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
  plot(detail$prep$history$date, e, type = "l", main = paste(m, "Innovations / Residuals"), xlab = "Date", ylab = "Residual")
  plot(fitted_values, e, pch = 16, cex = .4, main = "Residual versus Fitted", xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "Residual")
  qqnorm(e, main = paste(m, "Normal Q–Q")); qqline(e)
  plot(detail$prep$history$date, e^2, type = "l", main = "Squared Residuals", xlab = "Date", ylab = "Squared residual")
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
  ec <- regular_tail(e)
  if (length(ec) > 40 && var(ec) > 0) {
    plot_dependence(ec, paste(m, "innovations"))
    sq <- Box.test(ec^2, lag = 14, type = "Ljung-Box")
    cat("Squared-residual Ljung–Box: Q =", unname(sq$statistic),
      "; df =", unname(sq$parameter), "; p =", sq$p.value, "\n")
  }
}
for (m in names(detail$result$diagnostics)) {
  dtab <- detail$result$diagnostics[[m]]
  if (!is.null(dtab) && nrow(dtab)) {
    cat("Ljung–Box diagnostics for", m, "\n")
    print(knitr::kable(dtab, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE))
  }
}
}
```

```{r report-primary-coefficients, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(detail) && !is.null(detail$primary$fit)) {
 report_fit <- detail$primary$fit
 report_se <- sqrt(diag(report_fit$var.coef))
 report_coefficients <- data.frame(Term = names(coef(report_fit)), Estimate = as.numeric(coef(report_fit)),
   SE = report_se, `Nominal p` = report_p(2 * pnorm(-abs(coef(report_fit) / report_se))), check.names = FALSE)
 report_table(report_coefficients, "Selected primary-model coefficients", digits = 4)
}
```

For binary regressors, coefficients are conditional shifts in log(1 + sales);
$\exp(\beta)-1$ expresses a proportional change in that transformed conditional
level. These are associations, not causal promotion/holiday effects. Nominal
coefficient tests are approximate and become less reliable with remaining
innovation dependence; they are not used to delete terms automatically.

```{r report-primary-residual-plots, fig.height=6.1}
if (!is.null(detail) && !is.null(detail$primary$fit)) {
 report_fit <- detail$primary$fit
 report_e <- as.numeric(residuals(report_fit)); report_fitted <- as.numeric(fitted(report_fit))
 par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
 plot(detail$prep$history$date, report_e, type = "l", main = "One-step innovations", xlab = "Date", ylab = "Innovation")
 plot(report_fitted, report_e, pch = 16, cex = .4, main = "Innovations versus fitted", xlab = "Fitted log sales", ylab = "Innovation")
 qqnorm(report_e, main = "Normal Q-Q"); qqline(report_e)
 plot(detail$prep$history$date, report_e^2, type = "l", main = "Squared innovations", xlab = "Date", ylab = "Squared innovation")
 par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
}
```

```{r report-primary-residual-dependence, fig.height=3.9}
if (!is.null(detail) && !is.null(detail$primary$fit)) {
 report_innovations <- regular_tail(as.numeric(residuals(detail$primary$fit)))
 if (length(report_innovations) > 40 && var(report_innovations) > 0)
   plot_dependence(report_innovations, "Primary innovations")
}
```

```{r report-primary-ljung-box, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(detail) && !is.null(detail$primary$fit)) {
 report_diagnostics <- detail$primary$diagnostics
 report_table(data.frame(Lag = report_diagnostics$lag, Q = report_diagnostics$Q,
   df = report_diagnostics$df, p = report_p(report_diagnostics$p_value),
   `5% decision` = report_decision(report_diagnostics$reject_5pct), check.names = FALSE),
   "Primary-model innovation Ljung-Box tests", digits = 3)
 cat("The primary example ", if (all(report_diagnostics$reject_5pct)) "rejects no-autocorrelation at both reported lags" else
   if (any(report_diagnostics$reject_5pct)) "rejects no-autocorrelation at one reported lag" else "does not reject no-autocorrelation at either reported lag",
   "; passing a test would still not prove white noise.\n\n", sep = "")
 report_er <- regular_tail(as.numeric(residuals(detail$primary$fit)))
 report_square_test <- Box.test(report_er^2, lag = 14, type = "Ljung-Box")
 cat(sprintf("Diagnostic segment: %d days; mean innovation %.4f. First/second-half variances: %.4f / %.4f. Squared-innovation Ljung-Box p = %s.\n\n",
 report_diagnostics$n[1], report_diagnostics$mean[1], report_diagnostics$variance_first_half[1],
 report_diagnostics$variance_second_half[1], report_p(report_square_test$p.value)))
}
```

These plots retain evidence of autocorrelation, variance changes and unusual
innovations. Gaussianity is stronger than white noise, and a squared-innovation
test is only a variance-dependence screen, not definitive ARCH identification.
Internal missing residuals are not concatenated: ACF/PACF and tests use a
contiguous complete residual segment. Integrated roots are intentional and
excluded from ARMA stationarity/invertibility checks.

```{r representative-primary-residuals, include=FALSE}
for (r in final$representative_details) {

  f <- r$primary$fit; e <- as.numeric(residuals(f))

      "order =", r$primary$row$order, "\n")
```

```{r report-full-results, results='asis'}
report_allocations <- as.data.frame(table(model_summary$model))
report_allocations$Share <- 100 * report_allocations$Freq / nrow(model_summary)
report_table(report_allocations, "Selected forecasting methods", digits = 1,
  col.names = c("Model", "Series", "Share (%)"))
report_table(as.data.frame(table(model_summary$K[!model_summary$fallback])), "Selected Fourier dimensions",
  col.names = c("K", "Joint-model series"))
report_table(as.data.frame(table(model_summary$d, model_summary$D)), "Differencing specifications (fallbacks coded 0/0)",
  col.names = c("d", "D", "Series"))
report_lb <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(final$diagnostics, final$diagnostics$lag), function(x)
 data.frame(Lag = x$lag[1], Tested = nrow(x), Rejections = sum(x$reject_5pct), Percent = 100 * mean(x$reject_5pct))))
report_table(report_lb, "Aggregate innovation Ljung-Box rejection rates at 5%", digits = 1)
report_error_text <- paste(model_summary$warnings, model_summary$candidate_errors, model_summary$differencing_issue)
report_error_categories <- data.frame(Category = c("Nonfinite numerical start/optimization record", "Iteration/convergence record", "Bounded stepwise-search limit", "ADF/KPSS disagreement"),
 Series = c(sum(grepl("non-finite|nonfinite", report_error_text, ignore.case = TRUE)),
 sum(grepl("iteration|converg|code = [1-9]", report_error_text, ignore.case = TRUE)),
 sum(grepl("stepwise|nmodels|model.*limit", report_error_text, ignore.case = TRUE)),
 sum(grepl("disagree", model_summary$differencing_issue, ignore.case = TRUE))))
report_table(report_error_categories, "Recorded issue categories (series counts; may overlap)")
cat(sprintf("There were %d failed fitting attempts including recovered retries and %d rejected candidates. Warnings were recorded for %d series. Invalid selected ARMA-root checks: %d. ",
 sum(model_summary$failed_fit_calls), sum(model_summary$rejected_candidates), sum(nzchar(model_summary$warnings)),
 sum(model_summary$AR_root[!model_summary$fallback] <= 1 | model_summary$MA_root[!model_summary$fallback] <= 1)))
cat(sprintf("Forecast extrapolation flags: %d; large-innovation flags retained: %d.\n\n",
 sum(model_summary$forecast_extrapolation_flag), sum(model_summary$large_residuals)))
report_unresolved <- model_summary[model_summary$fallback & !model_summary$model %in%
 c("M0_all_zero", "M0_recent_inactive", "M0_constant", "M0_no_history", "M0_short_history"), ]
if (nrow(report_unresolved)) report_table(head(report_unresolved[c("series", "model", "failure")], 3),
 "Unresolved fitting-driven fallbacks", alignment = "p{3.8cm}lp{8cm}") else
 cat("No numerical fitting failures forced a series-level fallback; the zero/inactivity rules remain separate from recovered numerical failures.\n\n")
```

The nontrivial rejection rates above remain evidence of incomplete innovation
whitening, not a reason to claim model adequacy. Diagnostic flags and valid
unusual observations are retained. AICc/BIC and in-sample tests cannot establish
16-day forecast accuracy; structural changes, intermittent sales, holiday
irregularities and unpromoted reactivation remain limitations.

# 11. Kaggle forecasts

The horizon is **August 16-31, 2017**. The existing export writes only
`submission.csv`, with exactly `id,sales`, in original test order. No upload is
performed and no hidden target values are used.

Kaggle evaluates predictions using
\[
\mathrm{RMSLE}=\sqrt{\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^{n}
 [\log(1+\widehat Y_i)-\log(1+Y_i)]^2}.
\]
This metric motivates the log-scale target but cannot be calculated for the
hidden test outcomes inside the report.

```{r submission-inspection, include=FALSE}
cat("Final prediction count:", nrow(submission), "\n")
knitr::kable(head(submission, 10), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r report-submission, results='asis'}
report_table(data.frame(Check = c("Predictions", "Unique IDs", "Original test order", "All finite", "All nonnegative"),
 Result = c(format(nrow(submission), big.mark = ","), format(length(unique(submission$id)), big.mark = ","), ifelse(identical(submission$id, test$id), "Passed", "Failed"),
 ifelse(all(is.finite(submission$sales)), "Passed", "Failed"), ifelse(all(submission$sales >= 0), "Passed", "Failed"))), "Submission checks")
report_table(head(submission, 3), "Submission preview", digits = 4)
```

\clearpage

# 12. Conclusions and reproducibility

- Sales levels, weekday effects and variance vary over time; log1p compresses
  large values without discarding observed zeros. Holiday/promotion associations
  are contextual rather than causal.
- Weekly dependence is supported by complementary calendar, STL and ACF evidence.
  STL alone cannot identify a deterministic or stochastic trend.
- ADF/KPSS disagreements and bandwidth sensitivity are retained. Differencing is
  conservative and conditional on the specified deterministic components, not
  an automatic response to upward trend or weekly seasonality.
- Forecasts use joint regression with parsimonious SARIMA errors and all training
  history. In-sample AICc drives a bounded search; BIC, convergence and root checks
  supplement it. Explicit zero/inactivity/fitting fallbacks keep all series covered.
- Remaining residual autocorrelation and variance instability qualify nominal
  inference and model adequacy. A lower Kaggle RMSLE than the user-reported
  baseline **0.47053** is not guaranteed; no new score is claimed.
